card_summary: Cloudinary introduced the New Cloudinary Studio, enhancing image transformation capabilities. The New Cloudinary Studio's impact on live signal transport is minimal, as it focuses on image transformation. However, in hybrid live production scenarios, it may interact with JPEG XS compression, affecting signal integrity and latency in 12G-SDI or ST 2110 workflows.

Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Transport Latency by 30%

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their IP-cores for real-time video transport, allowing for reduced latency and improved signal integrity in live broadcast applications. This development is significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it enables more efficient use of existing 12G-SDI infrastructure. The technology is particularly relevant for live production environments where low-latency signal transport is critical.

Operational ROI

The introduction of JPEG XS compression has the potential to save broadcast operators significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs associated with satellite or fiber links. By compressing video signals in real-time, JPEG XS enables the use of lower-bandwidth links, resulting in cost savings of up to 50% per link. This is particularly relevant for live events where high-bandwidth links are often required to transport uncompressed video signals. The reduced bandwidth requirements also simplify signal routing, as fewer links are required to transport the same amount of video data.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as MPEG-2 or H.264 compression, JPEG XS offers significantly lower latency, typically in the range of 1-2 milliseconds, making it more suitable for live production applications. Additionally, JPEG XS compression is visually lossless, meaning that it does not introduce any noticeable artifacts or degradation of the video signal, unlike other compression algorithms. This makes it an attractive option for broadcast operators who require high-quality video transport with minimal latency.

Security & Integration

From an integration perspective, JPEG XS compression is designed to work seamlessly with existing broadcast infrastructure, including ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67 systems. The compression algorithm is also compatible with a range of transport protocols, including SRT and RIST, making it easy to integrate into existing workflows. In terms of security, JPEG XS compression is designed to meet the requirements of modern broadcast environments, with support for encryption and secure key exchange. The use of JPEG XS compression also enables compliance with relevant standards and regulations, such as SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy JPEG XS compression, broadcast operators will require IP-cores or software implementations that support the compression algorithm, as well as sufficient network bandwidth to transport the compressed video signals. A minimum of 1Gbps network bandwidth is recommended for HD video transport, while 10Gbps or higher is required for 4K or UHD video.
  • Compatibility: JPEG XS compression is compatible with a range of standards and protocols, including SMPTE ST 2110-20, NMOS IS-04, and AES67. It is also compatible with existing 12G-SDI infrastructure, making it easy to integrate into existing workflows.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming release of the JPEG XS standard is expected to include new features and enhancements, such as improved compression ratios and support for higher frame rates. Broadcast engineers should track these developments to ensure they are taking advantage of the latest advancements in JPEG XS compression technology.

The introduction of JPEG XS compression has significant implications for the broadcast industry, enabling more efficient and cost-effective live signal transport with reduced latency. As the technology continues to evolve, engineering teams should prioritize the evaluation and deployment of JPEG XS compression to stay ahead of the curve and take advantage of its many benefits.

Analysis: Cloudinary Studio's image transformation capabilities will impact broadcast workflows using JPEG XS codec, optimizing bitrate and latency for live streaming applications conforming to ST 2110 standards.
